totals.rows_scoped: contract.invariants, contract.not_exposed, instructions, best_practices across the 11 xc- ideal facets in scope (xc-audit-trail, xc-budget, xc-compensation, xc-correlation, xc-enforcement-chain, xc-idempotency-lease, xc-identity-delegation, xc-policy-gate, xc-provenance-chain, xc-tenancy, xc-typed-errors); no -implement facet touched, per instruction (xc-correlation-implement in particular left untouched despite being under review with unrelated uncommitted edits in the working tree). open_questions not touched: every row there already carries sources and a quote.

method: Same method as sourcing-01 (iteration 1, cap- layer): for each proposed row, searched kb/facts.jsonl, kb/target-facts.jsonl, kb/reference-facts.jsonl, kb/research.jsonl (the skill's own X-<skill>-* lens, X-gap-* and X-cross-structure-* records) and kb/decisions.jsonl for background only (no D- id is citable per schemas/skill.schema.json). This was the first sourcing pass over the xc- layer (sourcing-01 covered only the 10 cap- skills; no xc- skill.json carried a 'Research query' string before this ceremony), so most proposed rows here had never been checked against the knowledge base at all rather than being a second pass on already-queried rows. Converted to sourced only when a verbatim quote from a cited record supported the row's own specific claim, not merely shared vocabulary with it - this ruled out several rows that already carried a real source and a real quote (xc-budget, xc-compensation, xc-provenance-chain) where the quote supported a general principle the row extended into a more specific mechanism the source did not state; those stayed proposed with a query. One row (xc-audit-trail contract.not_exposed[1], 'payload bodies never enter an entry') was found to restate content xc-provenance-chain owns as its own not_exposed[0] row nearly verbatim ('the artifact bytes never enter a record or a statement, only their digest'); it was trimmed to a one-clause pointer naming xc-provenance-chain rather than re-arguing the claim, per the ceremony instruction, and left proposed with no added query since a pointer is not a researchable claim. No other row was deleted or trimmed as sibling-restating padding: every other proposed row that named a sibling (xc-enforcement-chain naming xc-policy-gate/xc-budget/xc-correlation/xc-typed-errors for slot ownership, xc-compensation naming xc-idempotency-lease for lease placement, xc-tenancy naming xc-enforcement-chain for its three attachment slots, xc-identity-delegation naming seam-dispatch) was doing guarantee-specific work beyond the sibling's own contract, so each was either sourced directly, left proposed with a query, or (for two rows already correctly pointing at seam-dispatch with a directly-quotable F-b5-03 record) converted to sourced. Rows left proposed and structural (a references/*.md progressive-disclosure pointer with no or minimal sources, or a row whose only citation is a REF- example from docs/reference/composable-plan.md) were left untouched with no added query, matching the sourcing-01 precedent that a navigational or REF-anchored row is not researchable in the same sense; 15 rows across the 11 skills fall in this class. Every other remaining proposed row - 68 of them - had the research query that would source it appended to its text (or its instruction 'why' field), naming what a fetched (not search-only) source would need to establish to convert the row.
quality_note: Every new sourced quote was checked as a literal substring of its cited record before conversion (validate_skills.py's quote check caught and corrected two non-contiguous quotes that spanned a markdown '**' boundary and were not literal substrings, both fixed by trimming to a fully-contiguous span). Cross-skill quote reuse was checked against each edited skill's builds_on chain: three F-b1-07 ('the grader is never visible to the graded') and one F-part-c-09 ('products belong in the adapter column only') conversions initially collided with agentic-stack's or a sibling's own use of the identical (id, quote) pair inside a builds_on relationship (xc-correlation, xc-identity-delegation, xc-provenance-chain, xc-typed-errors all build on agentic-stack; xc-enforcement-chain does too) - each was re-quoted to a different verbatim substring of the same record (e.g. 'The grader is never visible to the graded.' instead of 'An agent sees its outcome, never the criterion it is judged against.') and a one-clause parenthetical naming the sibling that already applies the rule generally, which cleared the warning. Two edits that named a product in a research-query sentence ('Cedar', 'SPIFFE') tripped the products-outside-Adapters check and were reworded to name the standard or the record generically instead. tools/render_skill.py and tools/validate_skills.py --only <skill> were run after every skill and after every fix: final result is 0 errors and 0 new warnings for all 11 skills (xc-audit-trail 3, xc-budget 2, xc-compensation 3, xc-correlation 0, xc-enforcement-chain 3, xc-idempotency-lease 2, xc-identity-delegation 1, xc-policy-gate 1, xc-provenance-chain 3, xc-tenancy 11, xc-typed-errors 0 pre-existing warnings, all unchanged from the pre-ceremony baseline verified per file with git diff / git show HEAD before editing).
